Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s a short, 10-question screen that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally and mentally during the past seven days of new motherhood. Everything you share stays confidential within our team, and our only goal is to make sure you feel heard and supported. We’ll take it one gentle question at a time, and you can answer in your own words. Ready to begin?

Over the last week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?
I’ve still been able to laugh—maybe not quite as easily as before the baby, but when my partner made that silly joke about diaper explosions yesterday, I definitely cracked up.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, I can still laugh—maybe not quite as quickly as I used to, but funny moments still get a chuckle out of me.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I do look forward to things—like my morning coffee once the baby settles, or taking her for a walk later. They’re small, but they still feel nice to anticipate.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
Not really. If she spits up right after I’ve changed her outfit, I might think, “Should I have waited longer to burp her?” but it’s just a quick thought—I don’t stay stuck on it.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason
A little bit. Sometimes I’ll suddenly wonder if her breathing sounds normal or if the room temperature’s OK, even though everything looks fine. It’s not constant, just a few moments here and there.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
No, I haven’t felt scared or panicky.
Things have been getting on top of me
Now and then, sure—like when she’s fussy and the laundry’s piling up, I feel a bit swamped. But it passes once I check off one or two chores or she finally naps.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, that hasn’t happened. I’ve been sleeping pretty well—mostly just broken up by her night feedings, but I drift back off easily.
I have felt sad or miserable
I wouldn’t say miserable. I’ve had a couple of moments where I felt a little down—like when she wouldn’t latch and I was tired—but it lifted quickly and I’ve generally felt okay.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
No, I haven’t cried. I’ve felt a bit teary-eyed once or twice from tiredness, but it never turned into actual crying.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, that hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 6: Screening Summary – Postpartum Period (EPDS not collected)

Symptoms endorsed  
- Mild, situational worries about infant wellbeing (Q4).  
- Occasional “swamped” feeling when baby is fussy/tasks accumulate; resolves with situational change (Q6).  
- Brief, self-limited low mood when feeding difficulties arise; no persistent sadness, anhedonia, or crying spells (Q8, Q9).  

Symptoms denied  
- Loss of interest/pleasure in usual activities (Q1, Q2).  
- Excessive self-blame or guilt (Q3).  
- Panic or pervasive anxiety (Q5).  
- Mood-related insomnia (Q7).  
- Self-harm ideation (Q10).

Pattern  
Transient, stress-responsive fluctuations in mood and coping; no sustained depressive or anxiety symptoms. No safety concerns elicited.

Screening significance  
Current responses do not indicate clinically significant postpartum depression or anxiety. Continue routine perinatal support and monitor at next contact.
